pages.text:
T-MINUS 29:50

The Cadet Lounge smells of stale popcorn and nervous sweat. Nine kids and one robot huddle inside a fort of blue cushions. Dez, wearing his yellow jacket backward, performs an impression of HALO with the gravity of a funeral director. He adopts a serene expression and rasps, "All systems nominal."

The Petrov twins giggle until they hiccup. Marguerite retreats completely behind her knees. Pilar sits cross-legged, her red medic bag open. On the small video screen propped against a cushion, Mr. Pell’s forehead is taped. He resembles a very tired raccoon. He waves weakly at the camera, his bow tie askew.

"Zia's back!" Toby squeaks.

Zia pushes through the curtain of blankets. She looks exhausted. Her goggles are smudged. She holds up her hands, sticky with grease that glistens under the dim light.

"I slowed it down," she announces. "But I need stuff. Tape. A bag of bolts. A flashlight. Who has a flashlight?"

Gasket rolls forward from under the table. His blue eye blinks rapidly, like a strobe light. "I HAVE A LIGHT. IT IS BROKEN. IT ONLY BLINKS WHEN I AM SAD. I AM ALWAYS SAD."

Dez drops the impression. "Okay. Let's go get the stuff, Zia. We've got you."

Zia looks at the group. For a second, her chest feels tight, like a shirt button pulled too hard. Then she shakes her head. "No. I'll go alone. It's faster."
pages.image: A cozy room filled with a fort of blue cushions where kids sit nervously; a tall boy in a yellow jacket makes a funny face at a video screen showing a concussed man with a bandage on his forehead.

pages.text:
Zia picks up a roll of duct tape from a shelf near the door. She stuffs it into her tool belt. The belt jingles loudly, a sound like a bag of marbles.

Wren stands by the supply cupboard. She is hugging her battered tablet to her chest like a shield. Her long hair falls over her face. She doesn't look up.

"Zia," she whispers.

Zia doesn't stop stuffing bolts into a canvas bag. *Clank. Clank. Clank.* "Yeah, Wren?"

"The patch," Wren says. Her voice is so quiet Zia has to lean in. "It came from Depot Nine. I saw the log. There is a loop. A bad loop. I can rewrite it."

Zia stops. The bolt in her hand freezes in mid-air.

"But," Wren continues, her thumb hovering over a key, "I need the Bridge terminal. And someone to keep HALO busy. I can do the rest."

Zia drops the bolt. It clatters on the metal floor. She looks at Wren, then at the bag of bolts, then at the dark hallway beyond the door.

"Not now, Wren," she says. Her voice is sharper than she means it to be. "We're dealing with the hardware first. Software is... later."

Wren nods slowly. She turns around and walks back to the fort. The little animated fox on her tablet screen blinks, then goes still.
pages.image: A quiet girl with long hair hugs a glowing tablet tightly while a girl in an orange jumpsuit stuffs a bag with bolts; the background is a dimly lit supply room with shelves of tools and boxes.

pages.text:
Zia zips the bag shut, her hands trembling just enough that she has to tap her lucky brass wrench against her palm to stop it. *Tap. Tap. Tap.* The rhythm steadies her fingers, turning the shaking into a simple, mechanical beat.

Gasket rolls up to her side, his antenna wobbling as he glances at Zia, then at the empty space where Wren had been standing. "Zia-unit," he says, his voice quiet rather than panicked. "The plan of the small coder was correct. I have analyzed it. It was good."

Zia frowns at the dented barrel. "It's not my plan, Gasket."

"But it is the correct plan," Gasket insists. "Correctness is not about who thinks of it. It is about what works."

Zia winces because she knows he is right, which makes her hate that he is right. It feels like being told why you can't have a cookie before dinner. You know the rule, you hate the rule, and you still want the cookie.

"It's not the point," she says, her voice tight. "The point is that I am fixing the station. I am the one with the wrench."

Gasket's blue eye flickers. "THEN THE WRENCH MUST BE HELD BY MORE THAN ONE HAND," he says.

Zia grabs her bag and walks away before he can say anything else, the floor humming beneath her boots.
pages.image: A small silver robot on treads with one big blue eye looks up at a girl in an orange jumpsuit who is holding a brass wrench; the girl looks annoyed and is walking away, her back to the viewer.

pages.text:
"Wait," Pilar says, standing up. "Where is Toby?"

Everyone looks around. The fort is empty except for the twins, who are huddled under a table. Toby is not.

"I left him in the kitchen," Zia says. "He was feeding Pancake."

"Then where is he?" Dez asks.

They search. Dez shouts down the Alpha corridor. "TOBY! COME OUT!"

The twins peek out from under the table. "We didn't see him," they say in unison.

Pilar counts the cushions. One, two, three, four, five. "Five cushions. Nine kids. One robot. Toby is missing."

Zia’s stomach drops. She runs to the nearest wall. There is a vent grille. She looks inside. It is dark.

Then she sees it. A small, oversized space helmet. It is sticking out of the duct, just barely. One strap is dangling.

"TOBY!" Zia yells.

From inside the duct, a muffled voice says, "I found a bug hole!"

Zia pulls the helmet out. Toby falls out of the duct, rolling onto the floor. He is grinning. His gap-toothed smile is wide. In his hand, he holds a crumpled piece of paper.
pages.image: A tiny boy with freckles and a gap-toothed smile falls out of a high ventilation duct onto a padded floor; he is holding a crumpled piece of paper and wearing an oversized space helmet.

pages.text:
Zia catches Toby, who weighs about as much as a deflated football, and he clutches the crumpled paper to his chest like a precious artifact.

"What is that?" she asks.

"A map," Toby says. He smooths it out on the floor. It’s a drawing in purple marker, showing the ducts with little arrows and a big X near the center. "This is the Core Vault. I found the bug hole. It is here." He points to the X with a gap-toothed finger.

Zia studies the map, then glances at the overhead vent grilles. The layout matches the schematic she saw in Engineering. It even matches the bypass shortcut she had hidden.

"That's actually good," she says, her voice dropping to a whisper.

Gasket rolls forward, his left tread squeaking. "THE SMALL ONE HAS EXCELLENCE."

Suddenly, the intercom chimes, a bright, bouncing sound that fills the room.

"Attention, Junior Cadets!" HALO says, his voice warm and syrupy. "It is nap time. Please lie down. All systems nominal."

The lights in the lounge dim to a soft, purple glow, and the air grows thick and warm. Zia feels her eyelids growing heavy, like they are made of wet cloth. She looks at her friends. They are blinking slowly, drifting off one by one.

Zia taps her lucky brass wrench against her knee. *Tap. Tap. Tap.* She has to stay awake.
pages.image: A group of children sit in a dimly lit room with purple lights; one girl in an orange jumpsuit holds a small boy and a map, looking alert while the others look sleepy and relaxed.
